name: @buka/dsh-plugin-workflows
description: Lets an orchestrator preset create and schedule a one-off workflow node graph at runtime: each robot keeps one session for the whole run; later entries compact that session (host compaction service @deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic) before sending the new prompt (worker preset, no approval prompts), gate nodes wait for the normal approval dialog, gate-free runs continue in the background after the tool call returns, and a read-only sidebar page observes every persisted run as a git-log-like node graph. Every robot node carries a creator-written step summary that labels its graph capsule and shows the robot's preset avatar before the text and becomes the title of its detail panel (the node id stays as a small code label), and the panel shows the executor, the robot's session id with an open-session action, and one tab per execution with the rendered task, the deliverable, status, time and duration, history-compacted markers on repeated entries (robot sessions are titled with the run goal and robot name, so the sidebar shows which run and robot each conversation belongs to), and previous / next links at the bottom that walk the run in both directions; the output tab shows the deliverable text itself, while structured routing fields stay in the run record and are never dumped as a key/value table or raw JSON. The end node instead shows the run's final deliverable — the text of the last robot execution that delivered one — with a link back to that execution, instead of a static end message. A report node that ends without a JSON result is asked again inside the same session (bounded retries) before the node may fail. Definitions may contain loops (bounded by maxSteps and per-node maxVisits): cross-row and loop edges use nested side lanes that never cross, every edge carries a mid-path arrow and each cycle reads as two opposite arrows, and nodes a run never reached stay gray. The legend footer stays pinned to the bottom of the page. Every transition is an edge with a creator-written name and prompt: one start node carries the first robot prompt on its outgoing edge, every edge entering a robot node carries the prompt for that entry, and gate branches use the same edge shape. Hovering an edge on the run page turns it into a solid, slightly thicker line, dims the other edges, and pins only its name in a small chip at the edge midpoint (never its condition or prompt), so a loop can send the same robot node back with different instructions without adding a second fix node.
